title: No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Natural Resources.
summary: The No AI Data Centers on Federal Lands Act prohibits the construction or operation of AI data centers on federal property, ensuring that public lands are not used for large-scale AI infrastructure. It also sets rules and enforcement measures so that the policy is followed and federal lands remain free of commercial data‑center development.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Referred to the House Committee on Energy and Commerce.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 seeks to regulate AI systems by requiring companies to regularly assess their algorithms for bias, safety, and transparency. It establishes mandatory reporting and enforcement rules so that AI technologies must be fair, accountable, and protect consumer interests.

title: Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on House Administration.
summary: The Protect Elections from Deceptive AI Act is a law designed to guard elections against the misuse of artificial intelligence. It would require that any AI‑generated content intended to influence voters be clearly identified and impose penalties for deceptive or manipulative AI use in the political process.

title: Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act
action: Ordered to be Reported by the Yeas and Nays: 44 - 0.
summary: The Protecting Families from AI Data Center Energy Costs Act aims to shield households from the rising utility bills driven by large AI data centers. It proposes regulations to limit energy consumption, incentivize renewable power, or require companies to offset costs so families are not disproportionately affected.

title: Homestake AI Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources.
summary: The Homestake AI Act of 2026 is a federal law aimed at regulating the development and use of artificial intelligence in the United States. It establishes safety standards, transparency requirements, and accountability mechanisms for AI developers, with enforcement and oversight by federal agencies.

title: A concurrent resolution expressing the sense of Congress that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge announced on March 4, 2026, reflects sound national policy to protect ratepayers in the United States, promote electricity affordability, and ensure that all people of the United States, including households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms, have access to reliable and affordable energy as artificial intelligence and data center infrastructure expands across the United States.
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Natural Resources. (text: CR S1618-1619)
summary: This resolution states that the Ratepayer Protection Pledge supports protecting customers from high electricity costs. It emphasizes the importance of affordable power for households, small businesses, schools, hospitals, and farms amid growing AI and data center use.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Environment and Public Works.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a law that aims to reduce the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It requires companies to measure and minimize energy use, carbon emissions, and waste from AI systems, while encouraging more sustainable practices and reporting.

title: PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The PROACTIV Artificial Intelligence Data Act of 2025 seeks to establish clear rules for how data is collected, stored, and used by AI systems, aiming to protect privacy and ensure responsible AI development. It outlines standards for transparency, accountability, and consumer rights related to AI-driven data practices.

title: Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Algorithmic Accountability Act of 2025 would require companies that develop or use AI systems to systematically test those systems for fairness, safety, and potential harms before they are released. It would also create a framework for ongoing monitoring, reporting, and corrective action to ensure AI technologies are transparent and accountable to users and regulators.

title: Children's Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: The Children’s Artificial Intelligence Toy Safety Act of 2026 sets rules that make sure AI‑enabled toys are safe, secure, and appropriate for kids, requiring manufacturers to meet strict safety and privacy standards. It also requires clear labeling and oversight so parents and regulators can verify that a toy behaves responsibly and protects a child’s personal data.

title: Youth AI Privacy Act
action: Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation. Ordered to be reported with an amendment in the nature of a substitute favorably.
summary: This act sets rules to protect young people's privacy when AI systems collect or use their data. It requires companies to get parental permission and be transparent about how children’s data is used, with strict penalties for non‑compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Physical Systems Coordination Act of 2026 is a U.S. law aimed at ensuring safe, responsible development and deployment of AI‑driven physical systems such as robots, drones, and autonomous vehicles. It establishes a national framework for collaboration among government, industry, and academia, setting standards, oversight mechanisms, and accountability measures to mitigate risks and promote public trust.

title: Expanding AI Voices Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Expanding AI Voices Act is intended to broaden the role of artificial intelligence in public and policy discussions. It focuses on ensuring that AI systems and their outputs are more transparently represented, fostering inclusive and diverse AI perspectives in decision‑making.

title: Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Data Center Moratorium Act is a law that stops the construction and expansion of large data centers that support artificial intelligence projects for a set period. It aims to curb the rapid growth of AI infrastructure, reduce environmental impact, and give regulators time to evaluate safety and privacy concerns.

title: Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026
action: Star Print ordered on the bill.
summary: The Future of Artificial Intelligence Innovation Act of 2026 seeks to promote AI research and innovation while balancing safety and ethical concerns. It sets forth regulations, funding mechanisms, and oversight to ensure responsible AI development and deployment.

title: NSF AI Education Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The NSF AI Education Act of 2026 establishes federal support for teaching artificial intelligence across K‑12 and higher education, providing grants to schools and universities to develop AI curricula and learning resources. It aims to create a skilled workforce by funding teacher training, student scholarships, and research projects that integrate AI into STEM education.

title: Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence-Ready Data Act is a proposed law that sets out rules and standards for collecting, organizing, and managing data so that it can be easily used by artificial intelligence systems. It seeks to improve data quality, make data more interoperable, and ensure that data is readily available to developers and companies building AI solutions.

title: Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Risk Evaluation Act of 2025 establishes a framework for systematically assessing the risks posed by AI systems, ensuring that developers and users understand potential harms. It requires regular risk evaluations, transparent reporting, and the implementation of safeguards to protect public safety and privacy.

title: CREATE AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The CREATE AI Act is a proposed legislative framework that seeks to establish comprehensive rules and oversight for the development, deployment, and use of artificial intelligence systems. It aims to promote transparency, accountability, and safety while fostering innovation and protecting privacy and public trust.

title: VET Artificial Intelligence Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The VET Artificial Intelligence Act is a regulatory framework that governs the development and use of AI technologies within the VET sector, focusing on safety, ethical practice, and accountability. It establishes standards for transparency, oversight, and risk management to ensure that AI tools benefit stakeholders while protecting public welfare.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Training Act of 2026 is designed to help small companies adopt AI by offering training programs, financial assistance, and clear guidelines. It encourages partnerships between government, academia, and industry so that small firms can build AI skills, stay competitive, and meet regulatory requirements.

title: Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Small Business Artificial Intelligence Advancement Act is designed to help small companies adopt and benefit from AI technology. It offers financial incentives, resources, and guidance to make AI more accessible and useful for small business owners.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed piece of legislation that seeks to regulate artificial intelligence by setting standards for safety, transparency, and accountability. It aims to protect consumers, encourage responsible AI development, and prevent misuse while promoting innovation.

title: LIFT AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The LIFT AI Act is a proposed law that aims to promote safe, fair, and transparent use of artificial intelligence by requiring companies to disclose how their AI systems make decisions and to test for bias. It also grants consumers the right to opt out of AI-driven services and mandates independent audits to ensure compliance.

title: Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Scam Prevention Act is a proposed law aimed at protecting people and businesses from deceptive or misleading uses of artificial intelligence. It requires companies to clearly disclose when and how they use AI, sets standards for responsible AI deployment, and imposes penalties on those who fraudulently mislead consumers about AI products or services.

title: States' Right to Regulate AI Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act grants individual states the authority to create and enforce laws governing the development, use, and deployment of artificial intelligence within their borders. It allows states to set standards and regulations aimed at protecting consumers, privacy, and public safety from potential risks associated with AI technologies.

title: Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Civil Rights Act of 2025 is proposed legislation aimed at protecting individuals from discrimination and bias by ensuring AI systems are designed, implemented, and audited to uphold civil rights principles. It seeks to establish clear standards, accountability mechanisms, and enforcement actions to prevent discriminatory outcomes in AI-driven decision-making.

title: Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence and Critical Technology Workforce Framework Act of 2025 seeks to build a skilled workforce for AI and related critical technologies, addressing current skill gaps and preparing workers for future roles. It proposes training programs, research funding, and industry partnerships to help the U.S. stay competitive and secure in AI development and deployment.

title: Artificial Intelligence Public Awareness and Education Campaign Act
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: This act establishes a national campaign to increase public understanding of artificial intelligence. It outlines funding, educational initiatives, and outreach efforts to ensure citizens are informed about AI’s benefits and risks.

title: TEST AI Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The TEST AI Act of 2025 is a proposed law that seeks to regulate artificial intelligence systems, aiming to set clear standards for safety, transparency, and accountability. It would require companies to disclose how their AI works and adhere to strict oversight procedures to protect users from potential risks.

title: Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025
action: Read twice and referred to the Committee on Commerce, Science, and Transportation.
summary: The Protection Against Foreign Adversarial Artificial Intelligence Act of 2025 establishes measures to shield national security from foreign influence over AI systems. It outlines requirements for detecting, disclosing, and mitigating AI tools that could be used by hostile actors, and imposes oversight and compliance obligations on developers and users.

title: SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Small Business and Entrepreneurship.
summary: The SBA Artificial Intelligence Utilization Act of 2026 establishes federal policies to encourage small businesses to adopt AI technologies, outlining eligibility criteria, tax credits, and grant programs. It also sets guidelines for responsible, ethical AI use, requiring compliance with data privacy, security, and transparency standards.

title: Self-Improving AI Monitoring Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Science, Space, and Technology.
summary: The Self‑Improving AI Monitoring Act establishes rules to oversee AI systems that can learn and change themselves over time. It requires monitoring, reporting, and compliance measures to ensure these autonomous learning technologies remain safe, transparent, and accountable.

title: Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act
action: Received in the Senate and Read twice and referred to the Committee on Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs.
summary: The Generative AI Terrorism Risk Assessment Act proposes to evaluate how generative AI technologies could be misused for terrorist purposes. It aims to identify and mitigate these risks by establishing assessment protocols and safeguards.

title: Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Science, Space, and Technology, and in addition to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Artificial Intelligence Environmental Impacts Act of 2026 is a proposed law that aims to assess and mitigate the environmental footprint of AI technologies. It likely requires companies to evaluate energy consumption, carbon emissions, and resource use associated with AI systems and implement measures to reduce negative environmental impacts.

title: Doctors Not AI Act of 2026
action: Referred to the Committee on Energy and Commerce, and in addition to the Committees on Ways and Means, and Education and Workforce, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned.
summary: The Doctors Not AI Act of 2026 is a proposed law that requires all medical diagnoses and treatments to be performed by licensed human doctors instead of automated systems. It sets rules and penalties for any healthcare provider that uses artificial intelligence to deliver medical care without proper human supervision.

title: Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act
action: Ordered to be Reported in the Nature of a Substitute by the Yeas and Nays: 37 - 7.
summary: The Full AI Stack Export Promotion Act aims to boost the United States’ competitiveness by encouraging the export of all components of artificial intelligence, from hardware and software to data and services. It seeks to provide incentives, streamline regulations, and support companies in accessing foreign markets for their complete AI solutions.

title: Open-Source AI Leadership Act
action: Forwarded by Subcommittee to Full Committee by Voice Vote.
summary: The Open‑Source AI Leadership Act is a proposed law that encourages the creation and sharing of AI technologies through open‑source platforms. It aims to make AI tools more transparent, collaborative, and widely accessible to researchers, developers, and the public.

title: Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Veterans' Affairs.
summary: The Responsible Artificial Intelligence for Veterans Act of 2026 seeks to ensure that AI tools deployed in veteran services are developed and used responsibly, emphasizing safety, transparency, and ethical standards. It establishes oversight mechanisms, requires impact assessments, and promotes training so veterans and providers can trust and effectively benefit from AI technology.

title: Advanced AI Security Readiness Act
action: Referred to the House Committee on Intelligence (Permanent Select).
summary: The Advanced AI Security Readiness Act is a U.S. law that sets out rules and best practices to help protect AI systems from cyber threats and ensure they are secure from design to deployment. It requires organizations to evaluate risks, adopt robust security controls, and report incidents so that AI technologies remain safe and trustworthy for users.

title: Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026
action: Referred to the House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform.
summary: The Eliminating Bias in Algorithmic Systems Act of 2026 seeks to reduce discrimination in AI by setting clear standards for data collection, model design, and outcome testing. It creates oversight bodies and penalties to enforce these standards and promote fairness in algorithmic decision‑making.
